pairs: when she had ceased to cry out to the Lord,
surrexit de loco in quo jacuerat prostrata ad Dominum.
she arose from the place where she lay prostrate before the Lord.
she took away from herself the haircloth,
et exuit se vestimentis viduitatis suæ,
and she put away from herself the garments of her widowhood,
and she anointed herself with the best ointment,
and she plaited the hair of her head,
et imposuit mitram super caput suum,
and she put a headdress on her head,
et induit se vestimentis jucunditatis suæ,
and she clothed herself with the garments of her elegance,
and she put sandals on her feet,
and she put on her little bracelets,
et omnibus ornamentis suis ornavit se.
and she adorned herself with all her ornaments.
And also, the Lord conferred upon her a splendor.
quoniam omnis ista compositio non ex libidine, sed ex virtute pendebat:
For all this dressing up did not proceed from sensuality, but from virtue.
et ideo Dominus hanc in illam pulchritudinem ampliavit,
And therefore, the Lord increased this, her beauty,
ut incomparabili decore omnium oculis appareret.
so that she appeared with incomparable honor before the eyes of all.
Imposuit itaque abræ suæ ascoperam vini,
And so, she appointed to her handmaid a wineskin,
And when they came to the gate of the city,
invenerunt expectantem Oziam et presbyteros civitatis.
they found Uzziah and the elders of the city waiting.
stupentes mirati sunt nimis pulchritudinem ejus.
being astounded, they wondered at her surpassing beauty.
they dismissed her to go forth,
Deus patrum nostrorum det tibi gratiam,
et omne consilium tui cordis sua virtute corroboret,
“May the God of our fathers give you grace,
and may he strengthen all the advice of your heart with his virtue,
et sit nomen tuum in numero sanctorum
so that Jerusalem may glory over you,
and your name may be counted among the holy and the just.”
Et dixerunt hi qui illic erant omnes una voce:
And those who were there, all with one voice, said:
Judith was praying to the Lord as she crossed through the gates,
Factum est autem cum descenderet montem,
when she descended the mountain at about the break of day,
the scouts of the Assyrians met her,
“I am a daughter of the Hebrews.
ideo ego fugi a facie eorum,
This is why I have fled from their face:
quoniam futurum agnovi quod dentur vobis in deprædationem,
because I realized that in the future they would be given over to you with pillaging,
for they hold you in contempt,
noluerunt ultro tradere seipsos ut invenirent misericordiam in conspectu vestro.
and they would never be willing to surrender themselves, so that they might find mercy in your sight.
For this reason, I thought to myself,
I will go to the face of the leader Holofernes,
so that I may reveal to him their secrets,
et ostendam illi quo aditu possit obtinere eos,
and show him by what means he may be able to prevail over them,
ita ut non cadat vir unus de exercitu ejus.
without one man of his army being slain.”
Et cum audissent viri illi verba ejus,
And when the men had heard her words,
et erat in oculis eorum stupor,
because they wondered exceedingly at her beauty.
Conservasti animam tuam, eo quod tale reperisti consilium,
“You have preserved your life by following such an excellent plan,
quoniam cum steteris in conspectu ejus,
that when you will stand in his sight,
et eris gratissima in corde ejus.
and you will be very pleasing to his heart.”
And they led her to the tabernacle of Holofernes,
And when she had entered before his face,
statim captus est in suis oculis Holofernes.
immediately Holofernes was captivated by his eyes.
Dixeruntque ad eum satellites ejus: Quis contemnat populum Hebræorum,
And his attendants said to him, “Who can hold the people of the Hebrews in contempt,
who have such beautiful women? So,
ut non pro his merito pugnare contra eos debeamus?
we ought to think it not worthwhile, for their sakes, to fight against them.”
Videns itaque Judith Holofernem sedentem in conopeo,
which was woven from purple and gold,
et cum in faciem ejus intendisset,
And, after she had gazed into his face,
adoravit eum, prosternens se super terram.
she showed reverence for him, prostrating herself to the ground.
And the servants of Holofernes lifted her up,
at the command of their lord.
